preamble: The voiced velar fricative [ɣ] is a weak consonant that is often lost between vowels or after a vowel, usually leaving a long vowel or a hiatus. In Turkish, the Ottoman and Old Anatolian consonant /ɣ/ (spelled ğ, earlier غ) disappeared: it lengthens a preceding vowel word-finally and before consonants, and it is silent between vowels. In Khalkha Mongolian, intervocalic Middle Mongol ɣ was lost and the flanking vowels merged into long vowels. In colloquial Modern Greek, intervocalic [ɣ] drops in common verbs such as λέγω > λέω.

examples.from: Ottoman Turkish طاغ (dağ) 'mountain', with consonantal ğ [ɣ]
examples.note: Final /ɣ/ was lost with compensatory lengthening of the vowel.

examples.from: Ottoman Turkish صوغوق (soğuk) 'cold', with consonantal ğ [ɣ]
examples.note: Intervocalic /ɣ/ is silent, leaving a hiatus.
Loss of intervocalic ɣ; the vowels merged into a long vowel.
